Running the targeted QA for `BATCH-12-DEV-02`. I’m starting by locating the touched files and running the scoped tests from the task notes so I can verify the delivered slice before deciding whether any local fix is needed.
The worktree is dirty in many unrelated areas, so I’m isolating review to the forecast contract/page files named in the task. Next I’m reading the exact diffs and the two scoped tests to verify the intended handoff behavior.
The scoped tests are present, and the target files look clean relative to `HEAD`, so this review is about validating the shipped behavior rather than reconciling an uncommitted patch. I’m checking the exact implementation points for risk-profile transformation and live-data export before I run the tests.
I’ve confirmed the new tests cover the raw-risk-profile fallback and freshness propagation. I’m reading the corresponding production paths now so I can judge whether the implementation actually matches the contract those tests assert.
The two requested tests pass. I’m doing one more targeted trace through the page-layer consumers to confirm there isn’t still a gap between the connector payload and the mounted dashboard merge path.
The page-layer merge now does derive `portfolioHealth` from raw `portfolioRiskProfile` in `app.js`, which closes the exact gap described in the handoff. I’m checking whether that page file is already covered by tests or if there’s an untested edge worth flagging.
The functional path looks correct, but the current tests stop short of the actual `app.js` merge logic that caused the original regression. I’m checking whether there’s an existing harness for `app.js`; if there isn’t, I may add one minimal regression test so the reviewed slice is proven at the consuming layer too.
I found a real QA gap rather than a behavior bug: the regression source was `applyLiveDashboardData()` in `app.js`, but there’s no automated test that exercises that consumer path. I’m reading the rest of that function now to see if a small extraction-style unit test is practical without broad harness work.
I’m adding one bounded regression test at the actual consumer layer in `app.js`. The implementation looks correct, but without this test the original failure mode could reappear while the current suite still stays green.
The regression test is in place. I’m rerunning the same scoped suite plus the new `app.js` consumer test to make sure the slice still passes end to end.
The new test exposed a problem in the test harness, not in app code: my first extraction method breaks on template-literal braces inside `applyLiveDashboardData()`. I’m tightening that helper by slicing to the known `window.addEventListener(...)` marker instead.
The consumer test is now executing; the remaining failure is just VM cross-context object identity in the assertion. I’m normalizing those values before compare, then I’ll rerun the suite.
The slice is passing with the added consumer-level regression test. I’m capturing the final test output to an artifact file and checking the exact repo delta so the review result has a concrete raw-output reference.
